---
title: "Setup Guides"
subtitle: "R, RStudio, Git, and GitHub, explained once and kept here"
---

These are the reference pages for the plumbing of the course: getting the
software installed, connecting RStudio to GitHub, organizing your work as
projects, and saving that work with commits and pushes.

We will walk through all of it together in class. These pages exist so that you
never have to reconstruct it from memory or from your notes. Bookmark this page.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
## Just want to get the homework in?

[**Doing a weekly exercise**](../weekly.qmd) is the short version: three
commands, start to finish. Come back here when you want to understand what
those commands are doing, or when something breaks.
:::

## Start here

If you are setting up for the first time, work through the guides in this
order. The first three are done **once**. The fourth you will use every week.

| | Guide | When |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | [Installing R, RStudio, and Git](install.qmd) | Once, before Week 1 |
| 2 | [Connecting RStudio to GitHub](github-setup.qmd) | Once (and again when your token expires) |
| 3 | [RStudio projects and cloning a repository](rstudio-projects.qmd) | Once per repository |
| 4 | [Committing, pushing, and pulling](commit-push.qmd) | Every time you work |

There is a fifth page that is not part of the sequence:
[**Error messages, decoded**](troubleshooting.qmd) is a lookup table of every
Git and GitHub error you are likely to hit, with what each one means and how to
fix it. Go there whenever something breaks.

## The one-time checklist

You are fully set up when all five of these are true:

- [ ] R and RStudio open, and `git --version` prints a version number in the RStudio **Terminal** tab.
- [ ] You have a GitHub account, and you can sign in to it.
- [ ] `usethis::git_sitrep()` shows your name, your email, and a stored GitHub token.
- [ ] You can open a repository in RStudio and see a **Git** tab in the top-right pane.
- [ ] You can commit a change and push it, and see it appear on github.com.

If any line fails, the guide that covers it is linked in the table above.

## If you get stuck

Read the exact error message, then look it up on the
[error messages page](troubleshooting.qmd). Nearly every Git problem people hit
is one of about a dozen errors, and all of them are listed there with fixes.

If that does not resolve it, paste the exact error (or a screenshot) into an AI
assistant and ask what it means. If you are still stuck after that, bring the
error text to office hours or email it. Please do not spend an evening fighting
the setup alone: it is not what this course is testing.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Not in this course? Welcome anyway

These guides are written to stand on their own. Anything specific to
GPH-GU 2182 is fenced off in a box labelled **In this course**; everything
outside those boxes applies to any R user setting up Git and GitHub. You are
welcome to link to these pages or adapt them for your own students.
:::
